Opening the summit, Mei Mei Lim, THE president for the Asia-Pacific region, highlighted Korea’s strong research capabilities, noting that the country invests more than 5 percent of its gross domestic product in research and development, making it one of the world's most research-intensive economies. However, she stressed that the country's next challenge lies not simply in increasing research investment, but in building stronger connections between academic discoveries, entrepreneurship and industry. items.title: 'Can we really catch it?' Teachers fear AI cheating; students urge tougher checks
items.title_zh: “我们真的能发现吗？”“教师担心人工智能作弊；学生呼吁加强检查”
items.summary: Fears of students cheating by using artificial intelligence (AI) technology are rattling classrooms before Thursday’s college entrance exam, leaving teachers increasingly unsure how to police an unprecedented threat and students worried about fairness. The anxiety emerged after the top scorer on a national tax accountant licensing exam admitted Sunday to using a miniature camera and generative AI to cheat. The confession reversed his earlier denials, which followed public scrutiny over his unusually high marks. Amid mounting alarm over AI-assisted cheating, the government is pursuing various measures, including blocking access to public Wi-Fi at College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) sites. Teachers who spoke to The Korea Times doubted the government’s measures would do much, saying the real question for proctors is whether they can actually catch cheating even when they suspect it. items.title: Gov't rules out postponing college entrance exam amid cheating fears

items.summary: An education ministry official reaffirmed Tuesday that the government is not considering postponing the national college entrance exam this week, a move called for by many amid widespread concerns over cheating using artificial intelligence (AI). The ministry has faced growing calls to postpone the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) scheduled for Thursday following a recent cheating scandal in the national tax accountant exam. "Postponing the CSAT is currently not being considered," the official said, reiterating the government stance against pushing back the exam to strengthen anti-cheating measures. Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin told lawmakers Monday it would be difficult to reschedule the CSAT as the move could lead to greater confusion. Concerns about AI-assisted cheating heightened after the top scorer of this year's certified tax accountant exam admitted Sunday to cheating on the test by using a miniature camera, a smartphone and generative AI. items.title: Technical hurdles complicate efforts to curb AI cheating
items.title_zh: 技术障碍使遏制人工智能作弊的努力变得复杂
items.summary: Korea is on high alert as cases of cheating using smart glasses and other artificial intelligence (AI)-powered devices unnerve students ahead of this year’s College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) on Thursday. However, technical hurdles are complicating efforts to prevent such devices from being used during the exam. The government is considering whether to disable public Wi-Fi services at all test sites during the exam, although questions remain over the effectiveness of such a measure. Most commercially available smart glasses require a separate internet connection to access AI features. As long as a paired smartphone has access to a mobile network, the glasses can continue to use AI functions without a Wi-Fi connection. Miniaturized cameras, which became a hot topic after the top scorer on the nation’s tax accountant licensing exam admitted to cheating using one connected to generative AI, can also connect to smartphones via Bluetooth or tethering connections, meaning that disabling Wi-Fi networks at test sites would have little effect. The university said it has topped the domestic rankings for four consecutive years since the revised edition was introduced in 2023, underscoring its research strength. Under the fractional counting method, which allocates credit among co-authors according to their respective contributions, 14.4 percent of the university’s publications ranked among the world’s top 10 percent most-cited papers, placing Sejong 157th globally and 81st in Asia. The indicator, compiled by the Centre for Science and Technology Studies (CWTS) at Leiden University in the Netherlands, measures the proportion of a university’s publications that rank among the top 10 percent most-cited papers in their respective fields and publication years. Sejong University also ranked No. 1 in Korea under the full counting method, which gives each participating university full credit for jointly authored publications. items.title: Cheong Wa Dae launches task force to combat AI-facilitated cheating
items.title_zh: 青瓦台成立工作组，打击人工智能辅助作弊行为
items.summary: The presidential office said Tuesday it has formed a dedicated task force to devise countermeasures amid growing public concerns over cheating with the help of artificial intelligence (AI). Cheong Wa Dae said its emergency response task force on AI-assisted cheating was launched under the guidance of chief of staff Lim Kwang-hyun and held its first meeting Monday. Discussions reportedly focused on measures to prevent AI-enabled cheating during Thursday's college entrance exam and respond to suspected cases. Lim instructed relevant staff, including officials from the presidential education secretary's office, the situation room and cybersecurity teams within the National Security Office, to remain on emergency duty through the day of this year's College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT). Cheong Wa Dae said it plans to keep the task force operational for the time being to develop countermeasures against AI-related cheating in next year's CSAT, as well as long-term strategies to address potential academic dishonesty involving increasingly advanced AI technologies.

Rep. Kim Min-seok's remarks came after the top scorer on the country's national tax accountant exam admitted to having used a microcamera and AI-assisted devices to cheat, raising concerns ahead of Thursday's nationwide college entrance exam. "We will prepare legislation to bar those caught cheating from taking the exam for up to 10 years," Kim said on the DPK's official YouTube channel. "Currently, those caught cheating on national exams face a five-year ban, while those caught cheating on the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) are barred from retaking the exam the following year," Kim said, referring to the nationwide college entrance exam. items.title: Prosecution warns of stern response to cheating with smart devices
items.title_zh: 检察机关警告将严厉打击使用智能设备作弊的行为
items.summary: The prosecution said Tuesday it will take stern action against cheating with smart devices on exams in the wake of a high-profile cheating scandal involving artificial intelligence (AI). The Supreme Prosecutors' Office said it instructed prosecutors to seek, in principle, formal trials against those caught cheating with generative AI or smart devices, effectively ruling out lighter measures like suspended indictments. Prosecutors will also actively seek arrest warrants and prison sentences in cheating cases that involve multiple people in an organized way or those that pose a major societal impact. The top scorer of this year's certified tax accountant exam admitted Sunday to cheating on the test using generative AI, sparking widespread outcry and calls for tough punishment against cheaters.

items.summary: Teachers are spending increasing amounts of time grading assignments and handling administrative work, leaving less time for students, but a Korean education technology startup believes artificial intelligence (AI) can help change that equation. Hyperlearning, an AI-powered education technology company specializing in assessment, is developing tools that automate grading, generate examination questions and provide personalized feedback, with ambitions to expand from Korea into Southeast Asia and the United States. Its co-founder and CEO Lim Chae-won believes AI should do more than make existing assessment methods faster. He argues that technology should fundamentally change how educators evaluate students and understand their abilities. “In the age of AI, the way we assess students and the very paradigm of educational assessment should be changed,” Lim said in an interview with The Korea Times. items.title: Islamic Military Coalition launches 2nd year of Saudi-backed counterterrorism program in Chad
items.title_zh: 伊斯兰军事联盟在乍得启动沙特支持的反恐计划第二年
items.summary: N’DJAMENA — The Islamic Military Counter Terrorism Coalition (IMCTC) launched on Monday the second year of its program for the Sahel countries in N’Djamena, capital of Chad, with support from Saudi Arabia.The four-week program, running from November 16 to December 11, 2026, aims to train 150 civilian and military personnel through a series of programs and workshops covering ideological, media, counter-terrorist financing, and military aspects.The launch ceremony was attended by Chad’s Minister of the Armed Forces, Veterans, and War Victims Issakha Maloua Djamous; IMCTC Secretary General Maj. Gen. Mohammed Al-Moghedi; and several military, security, and civilian officials from Chad. The second year builds on the achievements of the program’s first year, during which the coalition conducted 22 activities benefiting 2,300 people across five countries: Mauritania, Mali, Niger, Burkina Faso, and Chad. **media[2795492]**In his address, Minister Djamous expressed Chad’s pride in its membership in the coalition, saying the launch of the program’s second year reflected IMCTC’s continued support for Sahel countries in combating terrorism.He said the four areas of work addressed the evolving tactics of terrorist groups, including spreading extremist ideology, exploiting media platforms, securing funding, and carrying out operations. He added that training 150 civilian and military personnel would help strengthen the capabilities of Chadian institutions responsible for addressing these threats.The minister said terrorism remained one of the major challenges of the present era, crossing borders and undermining prospects for cooperation and stability. He stressed that the movement of terrorist groups across Sahel countries required regional and international coordination, affirming Chad’s continued commitment to collective security and defense efforts in line with its national priorities and regional cooperation.He expressed gratitude to Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman and Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman for the Kingdom’s role in establishing the coalition and supporting its operations. He also commended IMCTC’s focus on Sahel countries and its efforts to build the capabilities of their civilian and military personnel. **media[2795493]**For his part, Maj. Gen. Al-Moghedi said the launch in N’Djamena built on the first year’s achievements, which included 22 activities benefiting 2,300 people in five countries. He said the coalition worked closely with beneficiary countries to tailor its training programs to their priorities and institutional needs, enabling participants to apply the knowledge and skills acquired in their daily work.He noted that the coalition received continued support and direct oversight from Minister of Defense Prince Khalid bin Salman, who also serves as the Chairman of the Council of Defense Ministers of the member states of the Islamic Military Counter Terrorism Coalition (IMCTC).Al-Moghedi commended the Kingdom’s support for the Sahel program, saying it provided opportunities to exchange expertise, build national capabilities, and strengthen cooperation among member states in addressing cross-border threats. He noted that terrorist groups exploited extremist rhetoric to recruit individuals, used media platforms to spread propaganda, and relied on financing networks to sustain their activities.He said countering these tactics required a comprehensive approach encompassing the prevention of extremism, efforts to counter terrorist propaganda and financing, enhanced operational readiness, and coordination among civilian, security, and military entities. The program in Chad begins with workshops on the ideological dimension, focusing on understanding recruitment tactics and preventing extremism, followed by programs and workshops addressing media, counter-terrorist financing, and military affairs.Al-Moghedi added that the impact of training 150 civilian and military personnel over four weeks would extend to their respective institutions as participants shared their expertise with colleagues and applied their new skills in their duties.Through the launch of the program’s second year in N’Djamena, IMCTC continues its cooperation with Sahel countries through practical training for civilian and military personnel. The four-week program covers preventing extremism, countering terrorist propaganda, combating terrorist financing, and enhancing field readiness to help national institutions address cross-border threats.

items.title: Employers face up to six-month jail, SR100,000 fine for illegally assigning workers to others
items.title_zh: 雇主非法将工人转让给他人，最高可判处六个月监禁，并处以10万沙特里亚尔的罚款
items.summary: RIYADH — The Ministry of Interior affirmed that individual employers, who allow their workers to work for another employer or on their own account, face fines of up to SR100,000, imprisonment for up to six months, and a recruitment ban of up to five years.The ministry urged compliance with residency, labor, and border security regulations. It called on the public to report violations by calling 911 in the regions of Makkah, Madinah, Riyadh, and the Eastern Province and 999 in the rest of Saudi Arabia.

items.title: Environment ministry enforces sweeping ban on perennial forage crop cultivation
items.title_zh: 环境省对多年生牧草种植实施全面禁令
items.summary: RIYADH — The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture announced that a decision to halt perennial forage cultivation and transition to seasonal crops takes effect on Monday, Nov.16, across sedimentary shelf areas in the regions of Al-Jouf, Riyadh, Hail, Eastern Province, Qassim, and Tabuk.The ministry said the decision aims to curb the depletion of non-renewable groundwater, improve the efficiency of natural resource use, and conserve these resources, enhancing agricultural sustainability in line with the objectives of the National Agriculture Strategy.The ministry also outlined the seasonal forage crops permitted under the approved regulations for licensed farms and the expected reduction in non-renewable groundwater consumption resulting from the transition.Farmers wishing to cultivate seasonal forage crops can applyfor a license through the following link: https://naama.sa/services/details/92aed338-2639-43c5-9941-b1571fea63bb.

items.title: Saudi, Egyptian, and Qatari foreign ministers discuss regional de-escalation in phone call
items.title_zh: 沙特、埃及和卡塔尔外长在电话中讨论地区局势降级问题
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Minister of Foreign Affairs Prince Faisal bin Farhan held phone calls with foreign ministers of Egypt and Qatar on Monday.During the call, Prince Faisal and Egypt’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation, and Egyptian Expatriates Dr. Badr Abdelatty reviewed bilateral relations between the two countries and explored ways to further strengthen and advance cooperation across various fields. The two ministers also discussed the latest regional developments, underscoring the importance of continued coordination and consultation, as well as support for diplomatic efforts aimed at de-escalation to help consolidate regional security and stability.In a separate telephone conversation, Prince Faisal and Qatari Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani discussed the latest regional developments and ongoing efforts to promote de-escalation and maintain security and stability in the region.

items.title: Coalition intercepts 2 Houthi drones fired at Makkah and Riyadh regions
items.title_zh: 联军拦截了2架针对麦加和利雅得地区的胡塞武装无人机
items.summary: RIYADH — Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki, spokesperson of the Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen, stated that two drones launched by the terrorist Houthi militia were intercepted and destroyed in Makkah and Riyadh regions.Earlier on Sunday, the Coalition intercepted and destroyed two drones in the Makkah region and one drone in the Madinah region.

items.title: Saudi public transport buses carry over 25.5 million passengers in Q3 2026
items.title_zh: 2026年第三季度，沙特公共交通巴士运送乘客超过2550万人次
items.summary: RIYADH — The Transport General Authority (TGA) announced that public transport buses in cities across Saudi Arabia carried more than 25.5 million passengers in the third quarter of 2026, an increase of 3.6 percent compared with the same period in 2025. This reflects growing reliance on public transport and higher usage rates across the Kingdom's cities. Riyadh topped the list of cities with the highest number of public bus passengers, recording more than 19.29 million, followed by Makkah with more than 2.89 million and Jeddah with more than 1.19 million. Passenger numbers in the Dammam Metropolitan Area and Qatif governorate exceeded 789,000, while Madinah recorded more than 568,000. These figures reflect TGA's efforts to expand public transport services within cities and provide efficient, sustainable transport options that improve mobility, in line with the objectives of the National Transport and Logistics Strategy.

items.title: HR Ministry warns against violations of Support Labor Sector regulations
items.title_zh: 人力资源部警告不得违反《支持劳动力部门条例》
items.summary: RIYADH — The Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development has underscored the need for strict compliance with the regulations and requirements governing the Support Labor Sector, following the issuance of Ministerial Decision No. 112377, which introduces updates to the sector’s violations and penalties table. The amendments are aimed at reinforcing regulatory compliance, safeguarding rights, enhancing service quality, and ensuring the protection of all parties to the contractual relationship. The ministry noted that the violations and penalties table identifies violations, relevant provisions, and applicable legal procedures in accordance with the laws, regulations, and rules governing the support labor sector. The table includes violations related to recruitment activities and the provision of labor services, including recruiting workers or providing labor outsourcing services without obtaining the necessary licenses from the ministry. The ministry stressed that it will continue its field and electronic monitoring and inspection efforts to verify compliance with approved laws, regulations, and rules, and to implement the prescribed legal procedures in accordance with relevant provisions. The ministry called on all concerned parties to review the violations and penalties table and the regulations governing the Support Labor Sector through its official website, comply with their provisions, and report any violations through the approved official channels. It is noteworthy that the Support Labor Sector operates under the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development to manage, regulate, and advance the domestic and support labor ecosystem in Saudi Arabia.

items.title: King Salman appoints Al-Ruwaili acting Commander of the Joint Forces
items.title_zh: 萨勒曼国王任命鲁瓦利为联合部队代理司令
items.summary: RIYADH — Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman issued a royal order on Monday appointing Lt. Gen. Fahd bin Hamad Al-Salman as Advisor to the Minister of Defense for Military Affairs.The royal order also assigned Chief of the General Staff Gen. Fayyad Al-Ruwaili to assume the duties of Commander of the Joint Forces, in addition to his current responsibilities.King Salman, who is also Supreme Commander of all Military Forces, issued the order in line with the recommendation of Minister of Defense Prince Khalid bin Salman.

items.title: Saudi Arabia launches nationwide campaign to restore environmental balance
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯发起全国性运动，以恢复环境平衡
items.summary: RIYADH — The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture, through the Environmental Awareness Initiative, launched on Monday the 2026 Environmental Balance Campaign under the slogan “Balance Connects Us.” The campaign runs for 15 days, from Nov. 15 to 29, with participation from various agencies and centers within the environmental system, as well as government, private, and nonprofit sectors, and members of the public from all regions of the Kingdom. The campaign is based on a national vision that emphasizes that environmental protection is the responsibility of an interconnected system, in which the roles of the ministry and its specialized centers complement one another. Their efforts are united to safeguard natural resources and maintain the balance of ecological systems, unifying awareness messages and achieving the objectives of Saudi Vision 2030 and the National Environment Strategy in preserving natural resources and reducing all forms of pollution. The campaign promotes responsible environmental practices and the protection of natural, wilderness, and coastal areas, highlighting the interdependence of environmental elements through key issues such as wildlife and sustainable fishing; vegetation cover and habitat restoration; the marine environment, coral reefs, and sea turtles; infrastructure impact and environmental stewardship; waste and the circular economy; weather and climate monitoring; and enabling solutions and environmental financing. The ministry called on all government agencies, educational institutions, private-sector and nonprofit organizations, and the general public to engage with the campaign through digital platforms and on-the-ground initiatives. This is based on the principle that preserving environmental balance is a shared responsibility that unites individuals, organizations, and businesses in supporting environmental goals and ensuring the sustainability of the Kingdom’s natural resources.

items.title: Saudi Arabia elected to ITU Council for 2027–2030 term
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯当选为2027–2030年任期国际电信联盟（ITU）理事会成员
items.summary: DOHA — Saudi Arabia has been elected to the Council of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) for the 2027–2030 term, joining 47 other countries on the 48-member council, which oversees the union’s activities between major conferences. The election took place during the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference (PP-26), currently being held in Doha, Qatar, with the council comprising 48 countries elected from the union’s 194 member states. The election reflects the Kingdom’s international standing and its contributions to developing the communications, space and technology sectors, while strengthening its role in shaping the ITU’s strategic direction and building consensus on international priorities. It also reinforces Saudi Arabia’s efforts to bridge the digital divide, strengthen connectivity and expand access to technology and artificial intelligence, while leveraging its energy and computing capabilities to support a more inclusive digital future. Minister of Communications and Information Technology and Chairman of the Communications, Space and Technology Commission (CST), Eng. Abdullah Al-Swaha, congratulated Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman and Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman on the occasion. Al-Swaha said the Kingdom’s election reflects the international community’s recognition of and confidence in its leadership and contributions to developing the communications, space and technology sectors and strengthening international partnerships. He stressed that Saudi Arabia measures the value of technological progress by its impact on people’s lives and works with international partners to expand access to technology and help countries develop their digital capabilities. CST Governor Eng. Haitham Al-Ohaly also congratulated the Saudi leadership, saying the election reflects international confidence in the Kingdom’s contributions to the ITU and its ability to advance shared objectives. “Saudi Arabia plays a pivotal role in the ITU’s work by contributing to the development of its policies and strategies, building consensus among member states and exchanging expertise that supports the advancement of the communications, space and technology sectors,” Al-Ohaly said. He added that Saudi Arabia will work with its partners during the upcoming term to strengthen digital infrastructure, develop capabilities and support developing countries in expanding access to telecommunications services, helping bridge the digital divide and broaden access to technology and artificial intelligence. The ITU Council oversees the union’s activities between Plenipotentiary Conferences and monitors its policies, strategies and financial plans. Saudi Arabia joined the ITU in 1949 and was first elected to its Council in 1965. Over the past 77 years, the Kingdom has contributed its national expertise to supporting the union’s activities, initiatives, policies and strategies.
